To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the trajectories of HRQOL changes in breast cancer patients after radiotherapy are heterogeneous and that the pre-RT HRQOL assessment allows to predict the risk of falling into the low functioning cluster of HRQOL trajectories.
the diversity in changes of HRQL over a 1 year period after radiotherapy is substantial, and that the pre-radiotherapy assessment of HRQOL allows to predict the risk of “low functioning” clusters.
there is considerable diversity in the trajectories of changes of HRQOL domains over the 1 year after radiotherapy (i.e., there are different trajectories) in Norwegian breast cancer survivors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most important factors that determine changes in HRQOL in BC patients.
the identification of patients who are at risk of developing long-term problems after RT.
the diversity in HRQoO changes over the 12-month period after RT and may contribute to a better understanding of BC survivors’ long-term outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pre-RT assessment allows to identify patients who are at risk of experiencing a decline in HRQoLv.
the pre-RT assessment is a good predictor of HRQoLife changes in the first year after RT.
a subgroup of patients with low functioning and high symptoms after BC treatment is likely to be identified by the pre-RT HRQoL status.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to predict the course and level of HRQoO changes after RT in BC patients using the EORTC QLQ-C30 questionnaire.
the diversity of HRQoI changes in BC patients should be taken into consideration by the clinicians and the patients themselves.
the diversity in changes of HRqol over 1 year period after RT in BC patients is poorly understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diversity in HRQoOL trajectories should be taken into account in the development and implementation of tailored interventions for BC survivors.
HRQoL should be routinely monitored in BC survivors to detect the patients with the risk of developing low functioning clusters.
the diversity of changes in HRQL over the 1 year period after RT is considerable.
